claims.strategy: Geopolitical flash — buy crude on strike escalation
claims.crowd_belief: Markets fade oil from $98 to $90 on Iran 'end of current attacks' statement. Consensus treats SPR release as bearish supply injection.
claims.contradiction: SPR releases historically precede further escalation, not de-escalation. US now top oil exporter — structural supply disruption is widening, not closing. Crowd fading oil is the wrong side of the 2022 playbook.

claims.strategy: War premium + chip valuation compression — short rallies
claims.crowd_belief: Tech dip is a buying opportunity. AI thesis intact. Iran is a headline.
claims.contradiction: Dow -950 points on chip rout + war premium is not a dip-buying setup. Oracle tumbled on data center costs — AI capex cycle faces its first stress test. Until ceasefire materializes, rallies are exits not entries.

claims.strategy: Defense sector long — multi-front conflict locks budget increases
claims.crowd_belief: Defense stocks already priced the Iran escalation. Limited upside from here.
claims.contradiction: Three-front combat (US-Iran, Israel-Iran, Israel-Hezbollah) is NOT priced. US NATO cuts + simultaneous Middle East engagement = defense industrial base must expand. LMT/GD budgets structurally higher, not cyclically.

claims.strategy: Defense sector long — naval and ground systems demand accelerates
claims.crowd_belief: GD already benefited from Ukraine cycle. Iran is incremental, not transformational.
claims.contradiction: US naval operations in Hormuz + ground force posture in Iraq require sustained procurement. GD's shipbuilding and combat systems divisions see multi-year demand acceleration, not a one-quarter bump.

claims.strategy: Long US energy complex — structural market share capture
claims.crowd_belief: Oil sector is cyclical. Hormuz reopens, prices normalize, US loses export advantage.
claims.contradiction: European and Asian buyers signing long-term US crude contracts is permanent market restructuring. The US didn't just win a quarter — it captured customers who will take years to unwind. This is a structural rerating of US energy, not a cyclical trade.
